receipt.public_excerpt: ChatGPT-maker Open AI said Friday it has pushed out its co-founder and CEO Sam Altman after a review found he was "not consistently candid in his communications" with the board of directors.

evidence_items.explanation: Confirms the board fired Altman in November 2023 and gave lack of candour as the stated reason.

evidence_items.locator: Summary of WilmerHale review & findings, paragraph 4

receipt.public_excerpt:
WilmerHale reviewed the public post issued by the prior Board on November 17 and concluded
that the statement accurately recounted the prior Board’s decision and rationales.

evidence_items.explanation: The independent review found that the board's public statement accurately described its real reasons. This supports 'just like they said'.

evidence_items.locator: Summary of WilmerHale review & findings, paragraph 4

receipt.public_excerpt:
WilmerHale also found that the prior Board’s decision did not arise out of concerns regarding
product safety or security, the pace of development, OpenAI’s finances, or its statements to
investors, customers, or business partners.

evidence_items.explanation: The review rules out safety and pace-of-development concerns as the cause. An AGI breakthrough would fall under those concerns. The same passage attributes the firing to a breakdown of trust.

receipt.public_excerpt: Former OpenAI board member Helen Toner said that CEO Sam Altman was fired because he withheld information and lied to the board

evidence_items.explanation: One of the four board members who voted to fire Altman says on the record that the reason was candour and honesty with the board.

unresolved_gaps: The full WilmerHale report is not public. The review was commissioned by OpenAI's new board.
No source explicitly addresses AGI. The 'not AGI' part rests on the review ruling out safety and pace-of-development concerns.
